TNA BT 27/0420 p.68 (Harlech Castle, 9 Sep 1903) and BT 27/0448 (Walmer Castle, 9 Apr 1904). The index carries no forename; the image very often does. findmypast's tile viewer will not render in this browser. Two minutes elsewhere.

column4: DONE the same day. Act 1541, image ark 3:1:S3HT-XS9C-ZL. The parents are Don Luis Lerena Lenguas and Dona Julia Juanico, "naturales del E. Oriental" - both Uruguayan. See notes/the-uruguayan-turn.md.

column1: Search the Montevideo parish registers for Juan Carlos Lerena
column4: Uruguay, Registros Parroquiales, 1750-1930 on FamilySearch. A baptism in the 1840s-1850s and a marriage to a Maria before 1882. Opened by the 1866 Rosario act, which says the only Lerena in that parish was a native of the Estado Oriental.

column1: Find Luis Lerena Lenguas and Julia Juanico in Montevideo
column4: Their marriage, and his own baptism. If his father is the Don Luis Lerena who stood godfather by proxy in 1866, that is two generations from one act.

The shortest way at Juan Carlos Lerena. If Maria was a Lerena by birth, their marriage needed a dispensation for consanguinity - and dispensations are a thin volume, not a parish's worth of acts. Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, Marriage Dispensation Records 1856-1932, in the FamilySearch full-text corpus. Target window: 1875-1882.
